name: Helicorder Drum
desc: A seismograph drum turning under its stylus: twenty hours of trace wrap around a smoked cylinder and scroll away into the limb, the pen scratching live microseism at the front while earthquakes arrive as P-then-S bursts whose codas clip across three lines at once, and the helix steps down forever overwriting the oldest hour.

speed.doc: drum rotation rate (1 = ~5.7 s per revolution)

quake.doc: event magnitude — how far the codas clip across neighbouring lines

hue.doc: paper + chassis hue (offset from the style anchor)

style.doc: aesthetic: white stylus scratched through lampblack on a smoked drum / aged thermal paper with black ink and red hour rules / white trace on cyanotype / radically abstracted — the wiggle replaced by a filled amplitude-envelope ribbon

act.doc: multi-minute programme: quiet station watch / an earthquake swarm of small close events / rare huge distant teleseisms with long codas
